positions.as_written: Use mechanics to explain the pattern of the symptoms and to guide loading, not to explain why the patient has them.
Avoid attributing pain to a cartilage appearance, since the association is weak.
Offer loading based management before considering any mechanical correction for pain alone.
Reserve realignment for instability rather than for pain, because that is where the evidence sits.
Quantify exposure as well as intensity when taking a history, since cumulative load is the likelier driver.

Weigh the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations, because tolerance and adherence sit on that side of the balance rather than in the imaging.
